sections.overview: The tree’s name, Amphilophus calobrensis, is an older combination; current ichthyological catalogues accept Darienheros calobrensis. This freshwater cichlid is native to Panama’s Pacific slope.
sections.identification: Adults have thick lips, a long snout before the eye, eyes set high on the head and a slightly downward-facing mouth; dark bars break into irregular blotches rather than remaining evenly divided. FishBase reports up to 25 cm total length for a male or unsexed fish. Aquarium accounts describe mature males as often larger and deeper-bodied, with females smaller and less colorful. No dependable height, width or body-mass figures were located.
sections.habitat: The species is recorded in freshwater on Panama’s Pacific slope. It is reported from lakes, ponds and slower river reaches, especially around submerged rocky banks and crevices.
sections.diet: Detailed field studies of its diet were not located; aquarium references call it an adaptable omnivore, so those captive feeding notes should not be treated as a measured wild diet.
sections.behavior: Aquarium accounts describe territorial behavior and active digging in the substrate, especially around a potential spawning site; comparable wild field observations were not found.
sections.reproduction: Captive accounts report substrate spawning: a pair lays eggs on a firm surface and both parents guard them and the fry.
sections.ecology: Its known distribution is concentrated in one Panamanian Pacific-slope region, so the condition of those freshwater basins is relevant to the species’ persistence.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists Darienheros calobrensis as Vulnerable (VU), under criterion B1ab(iii), assessed in 2019.
